newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi stocks plough ahead in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi stocks plough ahead in busy trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabian shares ended last week 2.91 percent firmer in busy trade dominated by the services sector, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Saturday.
The index ended the week at 166.75 points from 162.04 a week earlier.
Of the 54 companies traded, 32 rose, 14 slipped and eight were unchanged.
The services sector accounted for 40 percent of trade, followed by banks, which made up 30 percent of volume, and industrials, with 16 percent.
BFA put turnover in the week at 8.58 million shares worth 1.69 billion riyals from the previous week's 8.76 million shares worth 1.24 billion riyals.
Riyad Bank was the most active share in the week, accounting for 17.6 percent of volume and 24.2 percent of value dealt.

The week's top gainer was Makkah Construction and Development Company for the second week running, rising 30.7 percent to close at 298 riyals. Saudi Industrial Export was also a leading stock, adding 9.2 percent to close at 130 riyals.
Riyad Bank was the week's third biggest gainer, rising 8.9 percent to 282 riyals.

Leading decliners was advertising and public relations company Tihama, which shed 5.6 percent to close at 68 riyals. Saudi Fisheries dipped 5.0 percent to 192 riyals and Beshah Agriculture lost 4.8 percent to end the week at 40 riyals. ($1=3.75 riyals)
